Subject: Long-context evals — post-call recap & next steps

Hi Chris / Priyanka,

Thanks again for the time today — great discussion. Quick recap from our discovery so we're aligned and to capture next steps: 

- Use case: automated summarization + executive TL;DR of long legal and policy documents (avg doc length ~60k–180k tokens; some up to ~250k).
- Key requirements: preserve factual accuracy, reduce hallucinations in summaries, deterministic truncation/segmentation behavior, and ability to run evals across a set of 150 canonical documents + prompt-suite.
- Scale: team expects ~5–10k requests/month in pilot, with bursts around quarter close.
- Security: data will be hosted on customer VPC for pilot; they need audit logs + SOC2 evidence.

What I'll send by end of week: 1) an initial long-context eval run we discussed (example outputs + summary metrics), 2) recommended model variants and quantization options for pilot, 3) the prompt set we used, and 4) a proposed short pilot scope and pricing sheet for commercial review.

Immediate question for you: is there a strict upper bound on acceptable latency for a single-document summarization? We discussed ~8–12s, confirm if that's the SLO target or if you need <5s for your UX.

Next steps:
- I'll drop the eval results + prompt set (attachments) by Thursday.
- Schedule a tech-deep-dive with our infra/product team (30–45m) to walk through integration and truncation strategies — does Friday 11/6 11am PT work?
- If pilot scope looks good, we'll follow with a SOW and reserved capacity proposal.

Thanks — looking forward.

Best,

Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 09:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Long-context evals — eval results + recommended models

Hi Chris / Priyanka — attached is the initial eval run and the prompt set we used (acme_long_context_eval_results_v1.csv, acme_prompt_set_v1.txt). High-level summary below.

Summary of the eval run (150 canonical docs):
- Models tested: redwood/long-64b-q8 (65k context), redwood/long-128b-q8 (140k context), open/llama2-70b-16k (baseline), redwood/concat-window-33b (windowed strategy).
- Metrics: factuality (ROUGE-FACT proxy), summary compression ratio, truncation loss (measured by token overlap to gold extracts), and mean tokens-per-second.
- Key findings:
  - For docs <=80k tokens: redwood/long-64b-q8 provided the best tradeoff of fidelity vs cost; median truncation loss <4% and 7–9s latency (on dedicated gpus).
  - For docs 80k–180k: redwood/long-128b-q8 retained fidelity with lower hallucination (truncation loss ~2.5%) but cost is ~1.8x vs 64b; median latency 12–18s.
  - For documents >180k tokens our windowed concat strategy (redwood/concat-window-33b) with overlap summaries + a final synthesis step preserved most facts while keeping cost lower — but it requires orchestration (2–3 staged requests).
  - Llama2-70b baseline at 16k context showed severe truncation artifacts as expected for this use case.

Recommended pilot approach:
1) Pilot model(s): redwood/long-64b-q8 for the bulk of documents, and redwood/long-128b-q8 for the largest docs that require single-request fidelity. Use concat-window approach as a fallback pattern for the rare ultra-long docs.
2) Prompt set: attached (acme_prompt_set_v1.txt) — we recommend the conservative-preserve-facts strategy (few-shot extraction prompts + explicit verification checks).
3) Quantization: q8 gave strong memory savings with minimal quality regression in our runs; we recommend q8 for pilot.
4) Truncation behavior: we recommend the concat-window approach with 20% overlap + extractive anchors for synthesis; that minimizes lost context and helps with faithful summarization.

Attachments included: acme_long_context_eval_results_v1.csv (metrics + sample outputs), acme_prompt_set_v1.txt (prompt suite).

Cost ballpark: for your pilot volumes (5–10k requests/month), expected per-request unit (average doc size 85k tokens) using long-64b-q8 on Redwood Dedicated is approx $1.20–$1.80 per request (includes compute, autoscaling overhead). Single-request long-128b-q8 runs approx $2.40–$3.20 per request. We'll refine during SOW.

Security & compliance: we can host pilot in your VPC, provide SOC2 artifact package, and enable audit logging. I've CC'd Rishi (Sales) and Lauren (Product) to coordinate SOW terms and the tech deep-dive on Friday.

Would you like us to: 1) schedule an ops/infra breakout at the same Friday slot to confirm VPC/networking, or 2) first run through the evaluation results in the deep-dive and then schedule ops? Either works for our team.

Best,
Marissa

Attachments: acme_long_context_eval_results_v1.csv, acme_prompt_set_v1.txt

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyanka Singh <priyanka@acme.ai>, Chris Zhang <chris@acme.ai>
Date: Sat, 7 Nov 2026 10:22:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: ACME pilot qualification & next actions

Team — summary and proposed internal next steps after the call and the eval delivery. Looping David for commercial/pricing coordination.

Qualification summary:
- Use case: high-confidence summarization of legal/policy docs (good ACV potential).
- Tech fit: positive — Redwood long-context variants cover most of their needs; windowed concat approach mitigates ultra-long docs.
- Risk flags: 1) potential quality regression when moving from q8->q4 if we try more aggressive quantization, 2) integration complexity for concat orchestration (requires client-side or middleware orchestration), 3) procurement timeline — customer needs SOC2 evidence and SOW approvals within 2–3 weeks.

Proposed next actions:
- Rishi: lead commercial outreach, prepare SOW + reserved capacity pricing. Attach draft pilot_scope.md and pricing_term_sheet.pdf.
- Lauren: own the tech deep-dive on Friday and bring infra/product to speak to concat orchestration options and latency tradeoffs.
- David: prepare a short pricing matrix for the two pilot flavours (64b-q8 vs 128b-q8) and options for burst capacity. Include the per-request ballparks Marissa sent.
- Marissa: book Friday 11/6 11am PT deep-dive (calendar invite already sent) and hand off attachments + Drive links to the customer.

Win criteria for pilot:
- Achieve <6% truncation loss on the 150 canonical documents (measured by our ROUGE-FACT proxy).
- Customer signs pilot SOW within 3 weeks.
- No major integration blockers for VPC deployment.

Flags for leadership: potential for dedicated contract if pilot succeeds; ACV estimate $250–500k ARR.

Thanks — will sync next week post deep-dive.
—Marissa

Attachments: pilot_scope.md, pricing_term_sheet.pdf
